items.prose: Raiders used a magnesium-rod thermic lance burning at 3,500°C to cut through the thirty-centimeter composite chrome-steel vault door. White-hot iron and alumina slag burned through three interior locking lugs, leaving a glowing fifty-centimeter jagged entry aperture.

Infiltrators flooded the heavy combination lock casing with four hundred liters of liquid nitrogen (-196°C). The ductile manganese steel shifted below its ductile-to-brittle transition temperature; two blows from a twenty-pound sledgehammer shattered the lock housing like glass.

A copper-lined conical shaped charge containing twenty pounds of Octol was positioned against the vault hinge line. The supersonic copper plasma jet punched a three-inch hole clean through two five-centimeter titanium-steel plates, severing the interior locking bar mechanism.

A water-cooled industrial diamond core drill bored a 12mm hole through the alumina ceramic matrix insert. The safecracker inserted an illuminated fiber-optic borescope to visually align the four wheel tumblers, opening the eight-ton door without triggering relockers.

A gravity-fed glass siphon dripped a 3:1 mixture of concentrated hydrochloric and nitric acid directly into the upper pivot hinge bearing. Over six hours, the acid dissolved the fifty-millimeter nickel-chromium pin into green sludge, allowing the door to be jacked off its lower seat.

A portable hydraulic rescue tool rated at one hundred tons was positioned inside the door reveal. High-pressure oil pump drove the spreader jaws outward with four thousand PSI, bowing the reinforced concrete jamb four inches until the heavy locking bolts slipped out of their strike pockets.

A close-proximity high-altitude nuclear EMP induced a 50,000-volt surge across the vault access control wiring. The current arc-welded the heavy magnetic locking solenoids in the retracted position, leaving the classified cipher safe permanently unlocked.
